our_title: Library link rules pass $(?) to $(AR): incremental shared-library builds drop every unchanged object
ran: ASan .so tree of base-combined: libscotch.so 1387 symbols; touch graph.c; make scotch -> 'gcc -shared -o libscotch.so graph.o', 3 symbols; top-level make scotch -> rc=2, 10 'undefined reference' (acpl.c:106 _SCOTCHusagePrint ...). Patched: touch graph.c; make -C src scotch ptscotch without removing any .so -> rc=0, 1387 symbols before and after, in both the 32- and 64-bit trees (verify.status).
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/Makefile:3583-3604 (libscotch, libscotcherr, libscotcherrexit, libptscotch, libptscotcherr, libptscotcherrexit); src/esmumps/Makefile:205-206 (libesmumps)
evidence: libscotch$(LIB) : $(LIBSCOTCHDEPS)\n\t$(AR) $(ARFLAGS) $(@) $(?)   with Make.inc/*.shlib: AR = gcc, ARFLAGS = -shared -o   (src/libscotchmetis/Makefile:222,235 use $(^))

fix_options.label: Use $(^)
fix_options.summary: Pass all prerequisites to $(AR) in the seven rules.
fix_options.tested: Incremental builds above; clean 32/64-bit builds; check/ptcheck/escheck.
fix_options.tradeoffs: For static archives 'ar -ru' re-inserts unchanged members (harmless).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: libscotchmetis/Makefile has done it this way since the 6.0 import; one-token change per rule.

fix_options.label: Remove the library before archiving
fix_options.tradeoffs: Also drops stale members from static archives, at the cost of a full re-archive each time.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Two lines where one suffices; he would take the libscotchmetis form.

fix_options.maintainer_fit: Obvious typo fix, same as his style fixes.

our_title: CMake emits the Fortran-template custom commands into every consuming target (duplicate rules under make -j)
ran: grep -l cmake_sed_test_scotch_mesh_build_f $W/cm/src/check/CMakeFiles/*/build.make -> test_scotch_mesh_build_f.dir and test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90_src.dir (pristine and patched); toy project $W/cmdup shows add_dependencies() does not change it.

fix_options.label: Restructure so that only the *_src target owns the rules
fix_options.summary: Executables should depend on the custom target and not list the generated file as a same-directory custom-command output (e.g. generate in a sub-directory or use an OBJECT library).
fix_options.tested: untested: design decision for the maintainer
fix_options.tradeoffs: CMake documents the duplicate-rule hazard; the race window here is a few milliseconds.

our_title: Fortran test template calls scotchfmeshinit/scotchfmeshbuild unsuffixed, so it cannot link with SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX
ran: cm64 (INTSIZE=64 IDXSIZE=64 SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_64 DETERMINISTIC=FULL): 'test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90:71: undefined reference to scotchfmeshinit_'; nm libscotch.so -> scotchfmeshinit_64_. dummysizes -s_64 on 'scotchfmeshinit##SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX(' -> 'scotchfmeshinit_64('; with -s -> unchanged. Patched: generated .f90:71 'call scotchfmeshinit_64(meshdat, ierr)', cm64 links; default build Fortran tests 3/3; Makefile chain check_scotch_mesh_build_f passes.
evidence: call scotchfmeshinit(meshdat, ierr)  /  dummysizes.c:282 subsFill ("##SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX", suffptr);  (same defect as G29's PS2-G29-4, found independently with -DSCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_pys; covered by patch 0011)

fix_options.label: Use the ##SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX placeholder
fix_options.summary: Append ##SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX to the two scotchf* calls.
fix_options.tradeoffs: none for unsuffixed builds (substituted by the empty string)
fix_options.maintainer_fit: The placeholder exists in dummysizes for this purpose since 2018 (75d50d7) and both build chains run dummysizes -s on the template.

fix_options.label: Skip Fortran tests under a suffix
fix_options.summary: if(BUILD_FORTRAN AND NOT USE_SUFFIX) around the test, as for esmumps.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Hides the configuration instead of testing it.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: He made Fortran tests work with suffixes on purpose (026e38e).

our_title: test_scotch_arch_build leaks the strategy created by SCOTCH_archBuild0() and every built architecture
ran: Pristine 7.0.17 test source compiled against INFRA/asan libs: ./t ./arch3.tgt -> rc=1, 'SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: 26544 byte(s) leaked in 240 allocation(s)' (stacks: _SCOTCHyyparse <- _SCOTCHstratInit <- SCOTCH_archBuild0 <- C_archBuild). Same in both combined-series ASan trees (make check stops there; make -k check: only failing target). Patched: make check_scotch_arch_build with leak detection on -> rc=0.
evidence: SCOTCH_stratInit (&stradat);\n  if (SCOTCH_archBuild0 (archptr, &grafdat, 0, NULL, &stradat) != 0) {...}\n  SCOTCH_graphExit (&grafdat);   (no SCOTCH_stratExit; main never calls SCOTCH_archExit)

fix_options.label: Free the objects
fix_options.summary: SCOTCH_stratExit after SCOTCH_archBuild0; SCOTCH_archExit at the end of each main loop iteration.
fix_options.tested: ASan run with leaks on passes; cm ctest.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Test hygiene he applies elsewhere (every other test exits its objects); needed for make check to pass under ASan.

our_title: Fortran mesh build test never releases its mesh and arrays, so it fails under LeakSanitizer

location_7_0_17: src/check/test_scotch_mesh_build_f.f90.in:78-79 (allocate), no scotchfmeshexit, no deallocate before 'end program'

fix_options.label: A: release the mesh and deallocate before the end of the program
